Notes: Valentine shows a steady activity pattern with three multi-month gaps, the longest a six-month pause from December 2021 to May 2022. The pause lines up with the end of a round of Python compatibility work by the same core maintainers, and nothing in the commits or README points to any internal trouble. It ended with a routine dependency bump, followed the same day by the same team resuming work on Python 3.11 support. The project remains active.

Notes: dd_functions has an irregular activity pattern with four multi-month gaps, the longest running 27 months from October 2022 to December 2024, roughly matching the end of a specific grant-funded period. GitHub's default branch view understates the project's recent activity, since real work has continued on a separate develop branch. Based on that default branch, the project currently reads as inactive.

The long-standing maintainer merged the fix and continued his own work right after. The project remains active.

The original author's work was tied to a specific research paper and stopped once that work concluded. Recovery came entirely from new contributors porting the codebase to a modern version of Julia for their own use, and the original author never returns in the post-gap commits. The project is currently inactive.

brainstorm3 is the only project studied with no inactivity gap of three or more months across roughly 15 years of history. Its cyclical pattern and large, sustained contributor base of over 100 authors set it apart from the single-author research code seen in the other projects. The project remains actively maintained today.

Gaia Sky shows a steady activity pattern with no meaningful inactivity gaps, aside from a single quiet month sitting inside otherwise continuous activity from one maintainer. This project is best described as having stayed essentially always active rather than having a real gap to interpret. It remains active today.
